- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.2) mid-period, model often overshoots early and then corrects — adjust forecast downward by 3–8% after 3–5 days of negative sentiment.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–2 days) — cap forecast rise to 3–4% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.5) and price is trending upward, model often fails to mean-revert — add a 1–3% downward bias toward end of horizon.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate the first 7–10 days; apply a 1–3% downward correction to early forecast points if sentiment is weak or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.0–0.3) over 5+ days, model often underestimates — increase forecast by 2–5% to compensate for mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model often misreads sentiment — reduce forecast by 1–4% to avoid overconfidence in positive sentiment.
